2 BYLAWS OF THE CALIFORNIA FOREST PEST Council (Currently Approved) A CALIFORNIA PUBLIC BENEFIT CORPORATION ARTICLE 1 OBJECTIVES SECTION 1. The California Forest Pest Council (herein referred to as the “Council”) is an organization, founded in 1951, of private and public forest managers, foresters, entomologists, pathologists, zoologists, biologists and others interested in the protection of forests from damage caused by animals, insects, diseases, and weeds. The objectives of the Council are to: Coordinate the detection, reporting, and compilation of pest damage. Evaluate pest conditions. Make recommendations on pest control to forest management and protection agencies and forest landowners. Review policy, legal and research aspects of forest pest management and submit recommendations thereon to appropriate authorities. Foster educational work on forest pests and forest health. SECTION 2. The Council is recognized by the State Board of Forestry as the advisory body to it with respect to forest health protection matters, and is a participating member of the Western Forest Pest Committee of the Western Forestry and Conservation Association. ARTICLE 2 MEMBERSHIP SECTION 1. Participation in the Council is open to anyone having an interest in forest health protection. There is only one class of membership and all members have the same voting rights and privileges. ARTICLE 3 OFFICERS SECTION 1. The Council shall elect from its membership for a two year term of office a chairperson, vice-chairperson, and secretary. A treasurer, conference chairman and editorial chairman will be appointed annually by the Council chairperson to serve a one year term. SECTION 2. Duties of the Chairperson. The chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Council and the executive committee and shall perform any other duties or functions authorized by the executive committee. The chairperson may appoint ad hoc committees and their chairpersons, as deemed necessary to assist in carrying out the purposes of the Council. The chairperson is a non-voting member of all committees of the Council. The Council Chairperson or other designated member of the executive committee or Council shall represent the Council, and report forest pest conditions and recommendations of the Council to the State Board of Forestry and appear on behalf of the Council before any other public bodies. The Council Chairperson or other designated member of the executive committee or Council shall represent the Council, and report to, the annual meeting of the Western Forest Pest Committee of the Western Forestry and Conservation Association. SECTION 3. Duties of Vice-Chairperson. In the absence of the chairperson, or in the event of his or her inability or refusal to act, the vice-chairperson shall perform all the duties of the chairperson. SECTION 4. Duties of Secretary. The secretary shall be custodian of the records and keep the original, and a copy of these Bylaws, a book of minutes of all meetings of the executive committee, standing committees and Council business meetings. The secretary should also keep a copy of all conditions reports, proceedings and other publications distributed by the Council. The secretary shall take minutes at the executive committee meetings and Council business meetings and distribute them to the executive committee within thirty days after the meeting. The secretary shall see that all meeting notices are distributed in a timely fashion and maintain the membership list. SECTION 5. Duties of Treasurer. The treasurer shall receive all payments, be custodian of funds of the Council, keep an account of all monies received and expended, and make commitments and disbursements authorized by the executive committee. At the annual business meeting and when asked by the executive committee, the treasurer shall make a full report covering the financial affairs of the Council. All funds, books, records and vouchers in the treasurer’s control should be subject to inspection and verification by the executive committee. The treasurer shall deliver to their successor all books, records, money and accounts pertaining to or belonging to the Council. SECTION 6. Compensation. Council officers shall serve without compensation. SECTION 7. Non-liability of Officers. The officers shall not be personally liable for the debts, liabilities, or other obligations of the Council. ARTICLE 4 COMMITTEES SECTION 1. Standing Committees. Standing committees are established as follows: - Animal Damage Committee - Disease Committee - Insect Committee - Weed Committee - Southern California Committee - Editorial Committee - Conference Committee - Executive Committee SECTION 2. Membership on the Animal Damage, Disease, Insect, Weed and Southern California Committees shall be open to anyone interested in the subject matter of the Committee. The Animal Damage, Disease, Insect, Weed and Southern California Committees shall elect annually, from their membership, a chairperson, and a secretary. SECTION 3. The Editorial Committee. The editorial committee shall be responsible for arranging for preparation and publication of an annual forest pest conditions report, proceedings of the annual CFPC meeting, and any other printed material of interest. The editorial committee will be chaired by one member representing the Director, California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection. The chairperson of the editorial committee will appoint the editor-in-Chief and any other members as needed. SECTION 4. The Conference Committee. The conference committee with the assistance of the Council shall plan and carry out an effective annual meeting of the California Forest Pest Council. It shall consist of a chairperson and members to handle the program, local arrangements, registration, publicity and other matters. The conference committee chairperson is appointed by the Council chairperson. The conference chairperson may then appoint all committee members. SECTION 5. The Executive Committee. The executive committee shall be composed of 15 members, as follows: 1. Executive committee chairperson - Council chairperson 2. Executive committee vice-chairperson - Council vice-chairperson 3. Executive committee secretary - Council secretary 4. Executive committee treasurer - Council treasurer 5. Member - animal damage committee chairperson 6. Member - disease committee chairperson 7. Member - insect committee chairperson 8. Member - weed committee chairperson 9. Member - Southern California committee chairperson 10. Members - editorial committee chairperson & editor-in-chief 11. Member - conference committee chairperson 12. Three members - at large, elected annually by the Council. SECTION 6. In the event the above membership of the executive committee does not include one member each representing the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, the Pacific Southwest Region of the USDA Forest Service, the University of California, and private industry, the Chairperson is authorized to appoint an additional person or persons as necessary to represent these organizations. SECTION 7. Each executive committee member may designate an alternate to represent their interests in the event they can not attend an executive committee meeting. SECTION 8. The executive committee shall coordinate all activities of the Council and its committees, and review recommendations for Council action made by the committees. It shall be empowered to take emergency action on behalf of the Council when necessary. No action may be taken on a matter which concerns the subject area of a standing committee unless the standing committee’s representative is present. SECTION 9. The following 11 members of the executive committee have voting rights for matters that the executive committee votes upon: 1. Executive committee chairperson - Council chairperson 2. Executive committee vice-chairperson - Council vice-chairperson 3. Executive committee secretary - Council secretary 4. Member - animal damage committee chairperson 5. Member - disease committee chairperson 6. Member - insect committee chairperson 7. Member - weed committee chairperson 8. Member - Southern California committee chairperson 9. Three members - at large Six voting members shall constitute a quorum if a representative from at least three of the following standing committees are present: animal damage, disease, insect, weed and Southern California. SECTION 10. Executive committee members shall serve without compensation. SECTION 11. The executive committee will serve as the advisory committee to the Board of Forestry. SECTION 12. Ad hoc committees may be organized and serve at the pleasure of the Council chairperson or the executive committee. ARTICLE 5 VOTING RIGHTS SECTION 1. Voting rights at the annual Council meeting and standing committee meetings will be established by attendance at the previous year’s Council or standing committee meeting, by attendance at a field meeting of a standing committee the current year, or by application to the Council secretary sixty days prior to the annual Council meeting. Any rights so established will remain valid for two years without further participation. Each member is entitled to one vote on each matter submitted to a vote by the members. Voting at meetings shall be by voice vote with majority rules. Election of Officers, however, shall be by ballot if the results of the voice vote are not clear. Each member of a standing committee shall vote for officers of only one committee. SECTION 2. Rosters. The Council secretary shall maintain and annually distribute to members of the executive committee: 1. Names and addresses of standing committee officers and of the full membership of the conference, editorial and executive committee. 2. Names and addresses of voting members thirty days prior the annual meeting of the Council. The animal damage, disease, insect, weed and Southern California committees shall prepare and maintain lists of members interested in their subject matter field, and send copies to the Council secretary. ARTICLE 6 NOTICE OF MEETINGS SECTION 1. The Council secretary shall prepare and distribute notices of Council meetings to the membership. SECTION 2. Standing committee chairpersons or secretaries shall handle distribution of notices of their meetings to those interested, sending copies also to members of the executive committee. ARTICLE 7 MEETINGS SECTION 1. Full Council Meetings. The full Council shall meet at least annually in November. The animal damage, disease, insect, weed and Southern California committees shall meet at least annually, and prior to the annual Council meeting, to review pest conditions in their subject area and to develop recommendations thereon to the Council. SECTION 2. Executive committee meetings. Regular meetings of the executive committee shall be held in February, August and November. In November, the executive committee shall meet just prior to the annual Council meeting, to review and coordinate recommendations being submitted by committees to the Council. SECTION 3. Conduct of Meetings. Meetings of the Council and committees shall be presided over by the appropriate chairperson. Meetings shall be governed by “Roberts’ Rules of Order”, revised version. SECTION 4. Minutes. The Council secretary shall prepare and distribute minutes of Council meetings within thirty days thereof to members of the executive committee. Copies of the minutes may be distributed to other members with notices or at any subsequent meetings. The Council secretary shall send copies of resolutions or other important material being submitted to external bodies, as a result of Council action, to members of the executive committee. The chairpersons or secretaries of the animal damage, disease, insect, weed and Southern California committees shall distribute copies of any minutes prepared of their meetings, and of any other pertinent correspondences and material, to the Secretary of the executive committee. ARTICLE 8 RESOLUTIONS SECTION 1. Resolutions. Resolutions are the means by which the Council advocates action or states positions on forest pest and forest health matters. Resolutions shall be introduced for discussion and adoption in the appropriate subject area committee. The Committee chairperson will forward the resolution to the executive committee for review. The Committee chairperson or his or her designee will then present the resolution at the annual business meeting so the membership may discuss and vote on the resolution. Resolutions shall include the names and addresses of intended recipients. Emergency resolutions may be presented to the executive committee for a vote if the resolution deals with an urgent matter that can not wait until the November meeting of the full Council. ARTICLE 9 FINANCES SECTION 1. Expenditures. The executive committee may authorize expenditures of Council funds. Checks, orders for the payment of money, and other evidence of indebtedness of the Council shall be signed by the treasurer, or Council chairman, or other person designated by the Council chairman. The Council chairman may authorize the reimbursement of reasonable incidental expenses in support of Council business. SECTION 2. Deposits. All funds of the Council shall be deposited from time to time to the credit of the Council in such banks, trust companies, or other depositories as the executive committee, or other person designated by the Council chairman may select. SECTION 3. Contracts. The executive committee may authorize any officer or agent of the Council to enter into a contract on behalf of the Council. Unless so authorized, no officer, agent, or employee shall have any power or authority to bind the Council to any contract. SECTION 4. Gifts. The Council chairman or the treasurer may accept on behalf of the Council any contribution, gift, or bequest for the charitable or public purposes of this Council. SECTION 5. Fiscal year. The Council fiscal year shall begin on the 1st of January and end on the last day of December. (Note: Document original misnumbered this as Section 3; corrected for sequence). ARTICLE 10 AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS OR ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION SECTION 1. Amendments. Changes to the Bylaws or Articles of Incorporation shall be presented to the executive committee for review and then presented to the full Council at the next regularly scheduled business meeting. The By-laws and Articles of Incorporation may be amended by a majority vote of the eligible voting members present at the business meeting.

SOP-001: Code of Ethics Draft The California Forest Pest Council (CFPC), founded in 1951, is a cooperative organization composed of individuals and organizations committed to the health and stewardship of California’s forests. Through education, scientific exchange, and collaboration, the Council promotes the understanding, prevention, detection, evaluation, and management of forest pests and other factors affecting forest health. The Council serves as a forum for the exchange of scientific, technical, and practical knowledge and encourages informed decision-making related to forest health management. The Council recognizes that healthy forests provide important ecological, economic, cultural, and social benefits and that effective stewardship depends upon collaboration, sound science, and consideration of diverse perspectives. To support this mission, members are expected to conduct themselves with honesty, objectivity, professionalism, and respect. This Code of Ethics establishes the principles that guide participation in Council activities and help ensure the Council’s work remains credible and effective. Principles Stewardship of Forest Health Members support the long-term health, resilience, and sustainability of California’s forests. Council activities shall be guided by sound science and responsible stewardship in understanding and managing forest pests and other threats to forest health. Scientific Integrity and Objectivity Members shall support the use of sound science, accurate information, and professional judgment in Council activities. Members shall distinguish among facts, interpretations, opinions, and uncertainties and shall not knowingly misrepresent or distort information. Professional Competence and Education Members participate in Council activities within the limits of their expertise and strive to maintain and enhance their professional knowledge and skills. Members support learning, mentorship, scientific inquiry, and the exchange of information among colleagues, students, and stakeholders. Objectivity Members shall strive to be objective, fair, and evidence-based in their participation in Council activities. Members shall clearly distinguish personal or organizational views from positions officially adopted by the Council. Collaboration Effective forest pest management and forest health stewardship benefit from diverse expertise, experience, and knowledge. Members shall foster open communication, constructive dialogue, mutual learning, and respectful consideration of differing viewpoints while engaging with others in a professional, courteous, and respectful manner. Integrity Members shall conduct themselves honestly, ethically, and in good faith. Members are expected to uphold the integrity and purposes of the California Forest Pest Council and adhere to the Council’s bylaws and adopted policies. Professional Conduct in Meetings and Communications Members shall participate in Council meetings and activities in a respectful, orderly, and constructive manner. Members shall follow the Council’s adopted meeting procedures and rules of order and contribute to fair and productive discussion. Disagreements shall focus on issues, information, and ideas rather than individuals. Communications related to Council business, whether verbal, written, electronic, or through social media, shall be conducted with professionalism, courtesy, and respect. Application This Code applies to all members, officers, committee participants, and individuals participating in activities of the California Forest Pest Council. Members are expected to uphold these principles while participating in Council meetings, committees, educational programs, publications, communications, and other Council-sponsored activities. Membership in the Council reflects a shared interest in advancing the understanding and management of forest pests and forest health. Members support the purposes and mission of the California Forest Pest Council by contributing to the exchange of knowledge, experience, and ideas and by participating in Council activities in a professional, respectful, and constructive manner. Violations of this Code may be reviewed and addressed in accordance with the Council’s bylaws, policies, and procedures. Adopted by the California Forest Pest Council on ______________, 20___.

PURPOSE AND SCOPE Purpose: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) operationalizes Section 9.01, Section 9.03, and Section 9.06 of the California Forest Pest Council (CFPC) Bylaws. It establishes formal internal fiscal controls, signature authority levels, contracting requirements, and grant management workflows to protect Council assets, prevent fraud, and satisfy federal, state, and private grant compliance parameters (including 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance and State of California grant terms). Scope: This policy applies to all Officers, Executive Committee (EC) members, Technical and Administrative Committee Chairs, project managers, contractors, and agents authorized to receive, hold, commit, or disburse funds on behalf of the Council. ARTICLE II. GENERAL FINANCIAL ADMINISTRATION Fiscal Year: The Council operates on a fiscal year beginning January 1 and ending December 31 (Bylaws § 9.05). Depository Accounts: All funds shall be deposited promptly in financial institutions approved by the Executive Committee (Bylaws § 9.02). Dual Control & Separation of Duties: No single individual shall have absolute control over the authorization, execution, and reconciliation of any financial transaction exceeding $1,000.00. Bank statements and reconciliations shall be reviewed quarterly by a designated Executive Committee member who is not an authorized signatory on the bank account. Prohibition of Cash Disbursements: All disbursements must be made via trackable electronic funds transfer (EFT), official bank check, or authorized Council credit instrument. Cash disbursements are strictly prohibited. ARTICLE III. EXPENDITURE APPROVAL THRESHOLDS To maintain operational agility while ensuring rigorous fiduciary oversight, commitment and disbursement authority thresholds are established as follows: Expenditure Level Threshold Range Required Authorization Verification / Documentation Tier 1: Minor Operational Up to $1,000.00 Single Officer (Treasurer OR Chairperson) Itemized receipt or invoice submitted to Treasurer. Tier 2: Intermediate / Contractual $1,000.01 – $5,000.00 Dual Officers (Treasurer AND Chairperson) Written contract, PO, or invoice signed by both Officers. Tier 3: Major Corporate Exceeding $5,000.00 Formal Majority Vote of the Executive Committee Approved EC meeting minutes or formal written consent record. Emergency Gap Allocation Up to $2,500.00 Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + Treasurer Emergency justification filed with EC within 5 business days. Note: Artificially splitting purchases or invoices to bypass higher approval thresholds is strictly prohibited. ARTICLE IV. GRANT EXPENDITURE AND REIMBURSEMENT POLICIES The Council frequently administers public and private grants (e.g., USDA Forest Service, CAL FIRE, foundation funds). All grant-related financial activities must strictly comply with the following parameters: Grant Budget Alignment: Expenses charged to grant accounts must be explicitly allowable, allocable, and necessary under the specific grant agreement and applicable regulations (e.g., 2 CFR 200 Subpart E for federal pass-through grants). SOP-006: Voting and Meetings ARTICLE I. PURPOSE AND GOVERNING AUTHORITY Purpose: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) operationalizes Section 5.05 (Action Without a Meeting & Electronic Voting) and Section 6.02 (Voting Rules & Ballot Voting) of the California Forest Pest Council (CFPC) Bylaws. It provides precise rules for conducting electronic meetings, asynchronous email votes, live digital polling, and confidential (secret) balloting to ensure full legal compliance with California Nonprofit Public Benefit Corporation Law (Corp. Code § 5211). Core Objectives: Protect members from peer pressure, institutional conflict, or political coercion during contentious votes. Maintain fluid, modern operational flexibility between annual meetings. Ensure strict verification of “one-member, one-vote” integrity across virtual and in-person settings. ARTICLE II. ASYNCHRONOUS EMAIL VOTES & WRITTEN CONSENT (§ 5.05) When emergency or routine operational decisions must be made by the Executive Committee between regular meetings, the Chairperson may initiate an asynchronous email vote or written consent action under Bylaws Section 5.05. Section 2.01 Unanimous Written Consent vs. Electronic Majority Vote 1. Unanimous Written Consent Action (§ 5.05a):** Pursuant to California Corp. Code § 5211(b), any action taken without a meeting and without advance meeting notice requires the explicit written consent (via email or signed ballot) of 100% of all voting members of the Executive Committee. 2. Electronic / Email Meeting Vote (§ 5.05b): In lieu of a physical gathering, the Chairperson may issue a formal “Notice of Electronic Meeting and Action.” Provided that a quorum (50%) of voting EC members submits written ballots within the designated response window, the action shall pass by a simple majority of those responding. Section 2.02 Standard Email Voting Workflow 1. Initiation:** The Secretary or Chair shall distribute the motion, supporting documents, and an official ballot via electronic mail to all EC members. 2. Discussion Window: A minimum window of forty-eight (48) hours shall be provided for electronic discussion prior to the ballot closing, unless an emergency gap expenditure (§ 9.01) requires a expedited 24-hour window. 3. Ballot Recording: All email responses (“Approve,” “Disapprove,” “Abstain”) shall be sent to the Secretary, compiled into a formal Voting Record, and filed permanently with the Executive Committee minutes (Bylaws § 5.05b). ARTICLE III. LIVE DIGITAL POLLING AND HYBRID MEETINGS For full Council meetings and Executive Committee sessions held via video conference (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Zoom) or hybrid formats: Roster Synchronization: Prior to calling a live vote, the Secretary shall verify that attendees match the official 2-year voting eligibility roster maintained under Bylaws Section 6.03. Standard Voice / Show of Hands Voting (§ 6.02a): Non-controversial motions may be decided by voice vote (“Viva Voce”), digital hand-raise, or unweighted chat response. Counted Voice Verification: Any eligible voting member may demand an immediate counted verification of a voice vote by a physical or digital show of hands. ARTICLE IV. CONFIDENTIAL (SECRET) BALLOTING PROCEDURES (§ 6.02b) To uphold the safeguards established during the 2026 Bylaws revision, any member has the procedural right to protect their vote from public view on contentious policy issues, elections, or sensitive resolutions.

SOP-007: Field Safety **ARTICLE I. PURPOSE AND GOVERNING AUTHORITY Purpose: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) operationalizes Section 4.06(b) (Conference Committee) and Section 7.02 (Full Council Annual Meeting) of the California Forest Pest Council (CFPC) Bylaws. It provides a structured framework for program development, registration management, venue contracting, continuing education accreditation, and field tour safety risk mitigation. Governing Scope: Applies to the Conference Committee, Technical Committee Chairs, Council Officers, event logistics staff, and all attendees participating in Council-sponsored meetings and outdoor field tours. **ARTICLE II. CONFERENCE COMMITTEE STRUCTURE AND TIMELINE Committee Composition (§ 4.06b): The Conference Committee shall consist of a Chairperson appointed by the Executive Committee, supported by designated coordinators for Program Agenda, Local Arrangements, Registration, Financial Accounts, and Continuing Education. Annual Planning Timeline: Planning Phase Target Schedule Key Deliverables & Action Items Phase 1: Location & Dates January – February Select host region, secure meeting facility/lodging contracts, and draft preliminary field tour routes. Phase 2: Program & CEUs March – June Finalize session topics with Technical Committee Chairs; apply for RPF (Registered Professional Forester) and PCA (Pest Control Advisor) Continuing Education Units. Phase 3: Registration Launch July 15 Publish formal Meeting Notice (Bylaws § 7.01), launch online registration, and distribute call for presentations. Phase 4: Site Scouting & Safety August – September Perform physical walkthrough of field tour stops; secure private land access permits and emergency medical contacts. Phase 5: Event Execution October / November Execute the Fall Annual Meeting, Technical Sessions, Field Tour, and General Business Meeting (Bylaws § 7.02). Phase 6: Post-Event Wrap-Up Within 30 Days Reconcile event revenues/expenses with Treasurer (SOP-002) and submit attendee rosters to Secretary (Bylaws § 6.03). **ARTICLE III. REGISTRATION MANAGEMENT & VOTING ELIGIBILITY Registration Fee Structure: The Conference Committee, in consultation with the Treasurer, shall establish registration fees to cover venue costs, catering, field transportation, and proceedings printing. Eligibility Roster Synchronization: Same-day physical and electronic registration desks must log attendee contact details, organizational affiliation, and professional capacity. Pursuant to Bylaws Section 6.01(a), attending the Annual Meeting or Technical Field Tour immediately establishes or renews the attendee’s 2-year CFPC voting eligibility. Ethics Affirmation Integration: Registration materials (online web forms and physical sign-in sheets) shall include the mandatory affirmation checkbox: “By registering, I agree to support the mission of the CFPC and abide by the Council Code of Ethics (SOP-001).” **ARTICLE IV. CONTINUING EDUCATION UNITS (CEU) ACCREDITATION To maintain professional value for natural resource practitioners, the Conference Committee shall submit educational agendas to accredited licensing bodies: California Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR): Submit pesticide laws/regulations and pest management content for Pest Control Advisor (PCA), Qualified Applicator (QAC/QAL), and Private Applicator credits. California Board of Forestry and Fire Protection: Submit forestry management, silviculture, and pest impact sessions for Registered Professional Forester (RPF) continuing education credits. Verification & Certificates: Maintain daily sign-in/sign-out logs at the meeting venue and field stops, issuing completion certificates to verified participants within fifteen (15) days post-event. **ARTICLE V. FIELD TOUR LOGISTICS AND SAFETY RISK MITIGATION Outdoor field tours frequently traverse active timber operations, rugged terrain, steep slopes, and remote wildland settings. The following safety protocols are mandatory for all field sessions: Section 5.01 Scouting, Permits, and Land Access 1. Private/Agency Access Agreements:** Written permission or land entry permits must be secured from private timberland owners, Tribal natural resource departments, or public land agencies prior to finalizing tour stops. 2. Transportation Safety: If passenger vans or buses are hired, vendors must provide proof of commercial liability insurance. Caravan driving routes must include designated staging areas to prevent roadside traffic hazards. Section 5.02 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) & Site Briefings 1. Mandatory PPE:** All field tour participants entering active forest management zones, logging sites, or hazardous terrain shall wear: * Hard hats (ANSI certified) * High-visibility safety vests (ANSI Class 2 or 3) * Sturdy, ankle-supporting work boots with non-slip soles * Eye and ear protection (when near operating equipment or active chipping/sampling) 2. Tailgate Safety Briefing: Before departing the initial staging area, the Field Tour Leader shall conduct a 5-minute safety briefing covering terrain hazards, active weather risks (heat/hypothermia), venomous species/poison oak, and vehicle convoy safety. Section 5.03 Emergency Medical Response Plan 1. First Aid Requirements:** Every field tour vehicle/group leader must carry a fully stocked Class B Industrial First Aid Kit, trauma dressing, and communication equipment (satellite messenger/Garmin inReach or cell booster when operating outside cellular coverage). 2. Medical Evacuation Routing: The Field Coordinator shall map the nearest emergency medical facility for each tour stop and identify primary emergency access points for local emergency services (CAL FIRE / County EMS). 3. Incident Reporting: Any injury or property damage occurring during a Council-sponsored event must be reported in writing to the Council Chairperson and Treasurer within twenty-four (24) hours for insurance documentation (Bylaws § 3.07).

SOP-008: Recordkeeping, Internal Controls & Audit Procedures 6.2 1. PURPOSE & REGULATORY COMPLIANCE This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines the California Forest Pest Council’s (CFPC) internal financial controls, audit protocols, and record retention rules. It is designed to be easily followed by volunteers while maintaining strict compliance with California Nonprofit Law, state grant guidelines, and federal Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200). 6.3 2. INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS To protect Council assets, prevent fraud, and maintain a clear audit trail, the following separation-of-duties protocols apply to all operations: 6.3.1 2.1 Cash Management & Purchasing No Cash Disbursements: The Council does not pay vendors, distribute stipends, or reimburse members with physical cash without Executive Committee approval. All outbound payments must be made via check, electronic funds transfer (EFT), or authorized payment processor. No Petty Cash: The Council does not maintain a petty cash box. For small, immediate event purchases (e.g., coffee, minor supplies), authorized members should use an official CFPC payment card or purchase out-of-pocket and submit a receipt for prompt reimbursement. Cash Receipts (Safety Gates): When physical cash is collected (e.g., event registration, merchandise), it must be counted by two individuals (including at least one Executive Committee member or event chair), logged immediately, and deposited intact into the CFPC bank account within three (3) business days. Reconciliation & Verification: Every payment requires an itemized receipt or invoice. The Treasurer reconciles the bank accounts monthly, and a non-signatory Executive Committee member reviews those statements quarterly. 6.3.2 2.2 Expenditure Approval Thresholds Authorizations for expenditures and disbursements are tiered as follows: * Under $1,000: Single Officer signature or electronic approval (Treasurer OR Chairperson). * $1,000 to $5,000: Dual Officer signature or electronic approval (Treasurer AND Chairperson). * Over $5,000: Requires a formal Executive Committee majority vote prior to execution. 6.4 3. AUDIT & REVIEW PROTOCOLS Audit procedures scale with the Council’s funding levels to balance accountability with practical operational efficiency: Tier 1: Biannual Internal Review (Standard Operations) For standard operations, the Executive Committee shall appoint at least two non-signatory members to conduct a biannual review of the Treasurer’s ledgers. This team will randomly sample transactions to verify receipts and ensure approval thresholds are being met. Tier 2: Independent CPA Audit A formal audit by a Certified Public Accountant is only commissioned when explicitly required by an executed grant agreement, or when CFPC’s gross revenue exceeds the California statutory threshold requiring an independent audit. Tier 3: Federal Single Audit Conducted only if the Council expends $750,000 or more in federal grant funds (direct or pass-through) during a single fiscal year, strictly complying with 2 CFR 200 Subpart F. 6.5 4. RECORD RETENTION SCHEDULE To maintain organizational continuity, records must be retained according to the following schedule: Permanent: Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS/State tax exemption letters, and official meeting minutes. 7 Years: Financial ledgers, bank statements, canceled checks, tax returns (e.g., IRS Form 990), and vendor invoices. 3 Years Post-Closeout: Grant records, data deliverables, and associated correspondence. These are kept for three years after the final grant expenditure report is submitted, unless the grantor requires a longer period.

PURPOSE AND GOVERNING AUTHORITY Purpose: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) operationalizes Section 9.01 (Expenditures & Disbursements) and Section 9.06 (Compensation and Reimbursement) of the California Forest Pest Council (CFPC) Bylaws. It provides precise rules for officer/agent expense reimbursements, travel allowable costs, and the administration of CFPC Student & Tribal Travel Scholarships for meeting attendance. Unsubstantiated claims or lavish/extravagant expenses will not be paid or reimbursed. ** Section 2.01 Vehicle Mileage and Ground Transportation 1. Personal Vehicle Mileage: Reimbursed at the current IRS Standard Mileage Rate in effect on the date of travel. Mileage claims must document point of origin, destination, and business purpose. 2. Commercial Ground Transport: Rental cars, taxis, rideshare services (e.g., Uber/Lyft), and airport shuttles are reimbursable when necessary for Council business. Compact/mid-size rental classes must be utilized unless pre-approved by the Treasurer for transporting meeting/field equipment. ** Section 2.02 Lodging, Airfare, and Per Diem Meals 1. Lodging: Reimbursed up to the single-occupancy room rate at the designated conference venue or current GSA/State of California per diem rate for the location. Itemized hotel folios showing zero balance are required. 2. Commercial Airfare: Economy/coach class airfare only. Premium economy, business, or first-class upgrades are non-reimbursable unless explicitly required for documented medical accommodations. 3. Meals and Incidentals (M&IE): Charged against GSA per diem rates for the specific travel destination. Meals provided directly by the CFPC conference (e.g., hosted field tour lunches or banquets) must be deducted from the daily per diem claim. ARTICLE III. TRAVEL SCHOLARSHIPS FOR MEETING ATTENDANCE To promote inclusivity, professional development, and student/Tribal participation (Bylaws Preamble & § 2.01), the Council may allocate budget for Travel Scholarships to attend the CFPC Annual Meeting or technical field sessions. ** Section 3.01 Eligibility Criteria 1. Annual Budget Allocation: The Executive Committee shall establish the total scholarship budget during the annual budget review under SOP-002. 2. Award Package: Scholarships may cover student registration waiver, shared hotel lodging, and up to $500.00 in travel/stipend assistance. 3. Selection Committee: Applications shall be reviewed and awarded by a panel consisting of the Conference Committee Chair, Vice-Chair, and one designated Member-at-Large. ARTICLE IV. CLAIM SUBMISSION AND DISBURSEMENT WORKFLOW To comply with IRS Accountable Plan rules, expense reimbursement packages must follow a strict submission window: Submission Deadline: All expense reimbursement claims and scholarship travel vouchers must be submitted to the Treasurer within thirty (30) calendar days following the conclusion of travel or event.
